w1.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints
w1.summary: Amazon SageMaker Inference now supports GPU partitioning with NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which divides one GPU into hardware-isolated partitions so you can run a different model in each or take a right-sized fraction of a newer accelerator. This post shows how two optional API fields place one model per partition, and what we measured against a whole older GPU.

w2.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick
w2.summary: As we built Amazon Quick, its agents grew from answering questions to taking actions, and the same primitives kept getting rebuilt under different names. This post shares the taxonomy we converged on — triggers, agents, capabilities, and learned context — found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When, What, Who, and How.

w3.title: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate
w3.summary: Learn how to build a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate that gives AI agents secure, metadata-driven access to an enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON file, with no per-dataset integration code.

w4.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 2
w4.summary: In Part 1 you built one governed agent. Part 2 scales the pattern to an enterprise: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes the single front door and redeems Okta's grant, Cedar policies bind each tool to the agent, a second agent runs on Amazon EKS, and AgentCore Observability traces every allow and deny beside Okta's log in Amazon CloudWatch.

w5.title: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
w5.summary: Greenlight Financial resolves more than 90% of up to 4,000 monthly security and risk cases without human intervention using Luna, a tiered multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post covers the architecture, episodic memory for continuous learning, and the expansion from SOC operations into financial risk triage.

w6.title: Extend Claude Code to remote sessions on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with security controls
w6.summary: Run Claude Code as a remote agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each coding task runs in its own isolated session in your AWS account, every model call goes through Amazon Bedrock, and the result comes back as a GitHub pull request you review and merge.

big_pour.headline: Election results may reshape the AI industry
big_pour.summary: Voters in recent midterm elections supported 40 out of 41 ballot measures to restrict data center development. This political shift could significantly impact how the AI industry expands its physical infrastructure.
big_pour.why: Political opposition to data centers may slow down the infrastructure needed for future AI growth.

explain.kid: People voted to stop big buildings that power AI, which might make it harder for companies to build more computers.
explain.pm: New local regulations on data centers following election results could create significant hurdles for scaling AI infrastructure projects.
explain.engineer: Increased restrictions on data center development across multiple jurisdictions could limit capacity and force changes to infrastructure deployment strategies.
